cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Mercury is the smallest planet, closest to the Sun, with no atmosphere and extreme temperature variations

cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Venus has a thick CO2 atmosphere causing a runaway greenhouse effect; it rotates retrograde

cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Earth is the only planet known to support life, with liquid water and a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere

cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Mars has a thin CO2 atmosphere, the largest volcano (Olympus Mons) and canyon (Valles Marineris) in the Solar System

cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Jupiter is the largest planet with the Great Red Spot (a persistent anticyclonic storm) and at least 95 moons

cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Saturn is known for its prominent ring system made of ice and rock particles

cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Uranus rotates on its side (axial tilt ~98°) and has a methane-rich atmosphere giving it a blue-green colour

cards.front: Recall a key point about Planets & Their Properties
cards.back: Neptune has the strongest winds in the Solar System (over 2000 km/h)

cards.front: What should you know about gcse astronomy exam tips — planets & their properties?
cards.back: 1. For Planets & Their Properties questions, define key terms before explaining processes 2. Use 'because' to link cause and effect in your explanations 3. Include units in all calculations and show your working for method marks 4. When evaluating Planets & Their Properties, consider both the quality of evidence and practical implications 5. For extended response questions, plan your answer: identify AO1/AO2/AO3 requirements first
Compare the properties of terrestrial planets and gas giants. [6 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of planets & their properties, including key astronomical concepts, observational data, and theoretical models relevant to AQA 8463, Edexcel 1AS0. AO2 (Application of Knowledge): Apply knowledge and understanding of planets & their properties to both familiar and unfamiliar astronomical contexts, using observational evidence

cards.front: Understanding Planets & Their Properties in GCSE Astronomy
cards.back: Planets & Their Properties is a key topic in GCSE Astronomy (AQA 8463 / Edexcel 1AS0) that requires understanding of both observational astronomy and theoretical concepts. You must be able to describe astronomical phenomena, explain the physical processes behind them, and apply mathematical relationships to solve astronomical problems.
